text:
jamal: hi team  first-day question: building runtime from source and link fails with relocation/PIC errors. any pointers?

jamal: build cmd: `./build.sh --targets=runtime -j12`

jamal: link error excerpt:
```
/usr/bin/ld: third_party/fast_kernels/libfastkernels.a(fast_kernels.o): relocation R_X86_64_32 against `.rodata' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

arya: welcome jamal! :wave: that message almost always means one of our static libs was built without -fPIC and you're linking it into a shared object. which distro and gcc are you on?

jamal: Ubuntu 22.04, gcc (Ubuntu 11.3.0-1ubuntu1~22.04) 11.3.0

marc: have you run `scripts/bootstrap_deps.sh`? the third_party builds are supposed to be built with our flags. also check `CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE` in the cmake cache.

jamal: i did run bootstrap but i also built a few third_party pieces manually earlier. `grep -R "-fPIC" build/third_party || true` returns nothing.

arya: try `file third_party/fast_kernels/libfastkernels.a` and `ar t third_party/fast_kernels/libfastkernels.a | xargs -I{} sh -c "file third_party/fast_kernels/{}"` to confirm objects are non-PIC. if they are, recompile that lib with `-fPIC`.

jamal: `file` shows: `fast_kernels.o: ELF 64-bit LSB relocatable, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), not stripped` (doesn't say PIC). the ar listing shows many .o files.

marc: `readelf -h fast_kernels.o` will show Type: REL (relocatable). To see PIC vs non-PIC, `objdump -r fast_kernels.o | head` sometimes shows relocations. but easiest is to rebuild with `CFLAGS=\"-fPIC -O2\"` or set `cmake -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON` for that target. we ship a helper: `scripts/rebuild_third_party.sh fast_kernels` which sets the right flags.

jamal: ran `scripts/rebuild_third_party.sh fast_kernels` and it recompiled. relink still fails but now different error: `undefined reference to cublasLtMatmul`.

arya: aha, two separate issues. the non-PIC lib was one blocker; now the linker says cublasLt missing which suggests the CUDA lib path isn't being passed for the new link step (maybe RPATH vs explicit link). what does the final link line show?

jamal: link line includes `-L/opt/cuda/lib64 -lcublas -lcudart -lstdc++` (no `-lcublasLt`). i tried adding `-lcublasLt` to `CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS` and retried but still undefined refs.

marc: check for multiple libcublas on system: `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` and `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda` and `which ptxas`. common cause: headers from one toolkit and libs from distro package.

jamal: `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` lists `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublas.so` (from distro) and `/opt/cuda/lib64/libcublas.so` (runfile). `/usr/local/cuda` -> `/opt/cuda-12.2`.

arya: then ensure the build prefers `/opt/cuda` paths: set `CUDA_HOME=/opt/cuda-12.2` and run `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/cuda-12.2/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` or use `-Wl,-rpath,/opt/cuda-12.2/lib64` in the link flags. also run a clean cmake: `rm -rf build && cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/opt/cuda-12.2`.

jamal: did that; now link succeeds and unit tests start up. :tada: thanks!

infra-bot: Hi jamal! Don't forget to complete the \"Runtime dev setup\" checklist in Notion and add your host CUDA/toolkit details to the onboarding doc.

jamal: will add a note to the README about rebuilding third_party with -fPIC and the CUDA runfile vs distro pitfall. appreciate the help.
_description: Onboarding thread: new runtime dev hits non-PIC static third_party lib causing relocation errors when linking shared runtime; team suggests rebuild with -fPIC/CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE, then encounters mixed CUDA installs causing missing cublasLt, resolved by pointing build at /opt/cuda-12.2 and setting rpath/CUDA_HOME
